clue.text: A few, in general, headed off, as you can see

indicators.note: something headed off has lost its head, so the first letter of the phrase before it goes

blocks.note: six, VI in Roman numerals, taken as a few
in general means as a rule, most of the time

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that, as a rule, only a few have lost their heads, as anyone can see.
explanation.walkthrough: Equating a few with six is loose, but the Roman numeral VI is what the wordplay needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done so that it can be seen is done by sight, which is the adverb's meaning.

clue.text: By way of a Channel bridge

blocks.note: via is Latin for by way of
a duct is a channel carrying liquid or air

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses by means of a bridge over the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes Channel look like the sea between England and France; here it is just any conduit.
explanation.definitionFit: A long series of arches carrying a road or railway across a valley is a type of bridge.

clue.text: Sluggish sae, perhaps, to go to one's bunk in

indicators.note: in at the end tells us the phrase before it goes inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: SAE, a stamped addressed envelope, written as letters
to turn in is to go to bed

explanation.surface: A sleepy person climbs into bed as if posting themselves in an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: An SAE is a stamped addressed envelope, sent so a reply can be posted back. 'Perhaps' signals that sae is only an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine once described those born under heavy, slow Saturn, so gloomy and sluggish in temperament.

clue.text: Cause disturbance in a private American gallery

blocks.note: taken as written
a GI is a US soldier, such as a private
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: A US soldier makes a scene in a London art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a famous group of art galleries in Britain, chiefly in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or shake something, whether a liquid or a crowd, is to create disturbance within it.

clue.text: Dye one doing wrong

indicators.note: doing something wrong garbles it, so the word before is put out of order

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
the five letters of doing rearranged

explanation.surface: A person who makes a mistake must die, or perhaps dye.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep blue colouring, extracted from a plant, has long been used to tint cloth such as denim.

clue.text: What one should do about key, that's Thomas's speciality

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the duty wraps round the letters that follow

blocks.note: your duty is what you ought to do
B is a musical key
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A note on what a keyholder should do, attributed to a man called Thomas.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe in the Resurrection until he had seen it, gives the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubiety is doubt, the quality famously associated with the apostle known as Doubting Thomas.

clue.text: Beginning a book

blocks.note: first meaning: origin, the start of something
second meaning: the first book of the Bible

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as starting to read; the book is the first in the Bible, which itself tells of the world's beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means origin or creation, and names the opening book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Binding with a cord a speciality

blocks.note: a cord is a string
ENT, ear, nose and throat, is a medical speciality

explanation.surface: Tying things up with a cord is someone's special skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Binding here is the medical sense, drawing tissues together, not tying up.
explanation.definitionFit: An astringent substance contracts body tissue, which older medical usage called binding, as in constipating food.

clue.text: Turn a plane into a building

blocks.note: first meaning: tilt an aircraft sideways to turn
second meaning: a building where money is kept

explanation.surface: A pilot steers an aircraft into a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots tilt the wings to change direction, and the same word names the premises of a lender.

clue.text: A pursuer is soon shaken off by clamour

indicators.note: shaken up and gone off, these words are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone being chased escapes a pursuer by making a lot of noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy state of loud laughter or uproar is a clamour, the noun matching the noun.

clue.text: Ship's engineers, after Patrick's heart

indicators.note: the heart of a name is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept
after tells us the engineers come later, following the selected letters

blocks.note: the middle three letters of Patrick
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A boat's crew of engineers are close to Patrick's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Engineers is more often RE, the Royal Engineers; here the longer abbreviation REME is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient Greek warship with three banks of oars on each side was a type of galley ship.

clue.text: Outdated, he meant to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A man who intended to change his ways is now behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes chewed by insects look old and shabby, so the hyphenated word figuratively means antiquated.

clue.text: Nymph's song

blocks.note: first meaning: the sea nymph who kept Odysseus on her island
second meaning: a Caribbean style of song

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a song belonging to a nymph; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Odyssey she is the nymph of Ogygia, and the word also names West Indian topical songs.

clue.text: Original sort of number, without its being over four

indicators.note: in a down answer, being over means sitting on top of what follows
without in its old sense means outside, so the number goes round the rest

blocks.note: a prime is a kind of number
read as it's, it is: the word it, being placed
the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: A note on an original kind of number that lacks something more than four.
explanation.walkthrough: Without here means outside, an old sense. Its has to be read as it's, it is.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive and original both describe the earliest, first form of something, before later development.

clue.text: The last sort of secrecy

indicators.note: to sort something is to rearrange it, so these words are put in a new order

blocks.note: all seven letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone calls secrecy the ultimate quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by furtive, covert means so as not to be noticed is a form of secrecy.

clue.text: Mishit a ball over its target. Excellent!

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the second

blocks.note: in golf, to top a ball is to hit it above its centre
the hole is what a golfer aims at

explanation.surface: A golfer fluffs a shot, but it lands right in the cup anyway. Excellent!
explanation.walkthrough: Top-hole is dated British slang for first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Old-fashioned upper-class British slang for first-rate or splendid, used as an exclamation of approval.

clue.text: An upset for me, a certain bloomer

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned upside down, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
one, as in one Mr Smith, means a certain person

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed at an embarrassing blunder they made.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer means a mistake on the surface, but in crosswords it is often a flower: something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: This woodland plant with cup-shaped flowers is literally a thing that blooms.

clue.text: Trying hard to leave film about a con trick

indicators.note: the letter that leaves is dropped from the film's title

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
The Sting is the 1973 film about con men

explanation.surface: Someone tries hard to walk out of a film about a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trying hard' reads as one phrase; the definition is Trying alone, and hard is the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A trying situation is one that is demanding and exhausting, the adjective meaning a severe test of patience.

clue.text: Henceforth I'm blessed if HI provide such handy protection

indicators.note: the opening words provide the letters, which sit inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the end of the first word into the next two
surface padding, garbled in the scan

explanation.surface: Someone vows to be blessed if they ever supply such useful cover again.
explanation.walkthrough: The text around if HI is garbled in the scan, but the hidden letters are clear.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cap worn on a fingertip while sewing literally protects the hand from the needle.

clue.text: Model's about the right height

indicators.note: about means around, so the model surrounds the next letter

blocks.note: a statue is a sculpted model of a figure
R is short for right

explanation.surface: A fashion model is said to be just the right height.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's stature is how tall they stand, which is literally their bodily height.

clue.text: Shooting a chap outside, one missing the temple

indicators.note: the chap goes outside, wrapping round what follows
with one missing, the Roman numeral for one is dropped

blocks.note: a guy is a man
the Inner Temple, one of London's Inns of Court

explanation.surface: A man is shot outside a temple while someone is unaccounted for.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inner Temple is one of the four Inns of Court, the London societies that train barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunnery is the operation and firing of large guns, so the noun shooting fits it.

clue.text: Calvanistic doctrine throws ten into despair

indicators.note: throwing things scatters them, so the following words are jumbled

blocks.note: all fourteen letters of these words

explanation.surface: A bleak religious teaching drives ten people to hopelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvanistic is the printed misspelling of Calvinistic, after the reformer John Calvin.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin taught that God has decided in advance who will be saved, the central idea of his theology.

clue.text: A fuss about nothing, girl

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the following words are read from the end

blocks.note: the letter O looks like zero
Dot is a girl's name, short for Dorothy

explanation.surface: A row over nothing, involving a girl: the title Much Ado About Nothing hovers here.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or bother is a fuss, the British informal noun with the same meaning.

clue.text: The drum in point is a musical instrument

blocks.note: a tambour is a drum
taken as written
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A drum is described as being to the point, a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies the answer is itself a drum; in fact the whole wordplay builds a jingling hand percussion instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A small frame drum fitted with jingles, shaken or struck by hand, is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Flower cut to a point. . .

blocks.note: to sever is to cut
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A cut flower trimmed to a point at its stem.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, running from Wales into the Bristol Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is often a river, something that flows, and this is a major British one.

clue.text: ...badly cut, see

blocks.note: to sever is to cut
Ely is a cathedral city, the seat of a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the flower was badly cut, look.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely in Cambridgeshire is a favourite crossword one.
explanation.definitionFit: Severely injured and badly injured are the same, both adverbs meaning seriously or to a grave degree.
